pictureQuestions.prompt: At the shallowest occupied level, the picture has items 6 and −6. What sum is returned?

choices.feedback: Correct. 6 + (−6) cancels to zero.
Negative values are real items and must be included.
The −5 sits one level deeper and is ignored.
Zero is a valid sum; it does not mean the level had no items.

nodeQuestion.prompt: What gets its own node in the pile's nesting tree?

choices.label: Every array box and every integer item; the outer array is the root.
choices.feedback: Correct. Box nodes determine depth, and integer leaves are the values that may be summed.

choices.label: Only integers, labeled with their final depth.
choices.feedback: That records an answer after depth is known but does not model how recursion discovers depth through boxes.

choices.label: Every integer and only arrays that contain at least one integer somewhere below.
choices.feedback: Empty arrays still occupy positions and matter when finding whether a level has items.

choices.label: One node per depth, holding all item values found there.
choices.feedback: That collapses separate branches and hides parent-child nesting.

edgeQuestion.prompt: Which direct containment relationship becomes an edge?

choices.label: An array connects to each item or inner array directly inside it.
choices.feedback: Correct. Crossing one such edge moves to contents one level deeper.

choices.label: Connect the root directly to every item at the shallowest occupied depth.
choices.feedback: That uses the result to redraw the input and removes deeper branches needed to find that result.

choices.label: Every outer array connects directly to all integers anywhere inside it.
choices.feedback: Skipping intermediate boxes makes deep items appear too shallow.

choices.label: Connect integers that appear next to each other when the input is printed.
choices.feedback: Printed neighbors may live in different boxes. Containment, not text position, defines edges.

pictureQuestions.prompt: With `k=6`, secure lines leave components `{0,1,2}`, `{3,4}`, and `{5}`. How many networks?

choices.feedback: Correct. The qualifying lines form exactly three connected components.
Scores 5 and 4 are below k and cannot bridge the three groups.
Offices joined by secure paths belong to the same network.

nodeQuestion.prompt: What should each node represent in the courier network?

choices.label: Every office index `0` through `n−1`, even one trusted by nobody.
choices.feedback: Correct. An isolated office forms its own one-office network.

choices.label: Only offices with a qualifying trust score with another office.

edgeQuestion.prompt: When should offices i and j share an edge?

choices.label: Connect different offices i and j when trust[i][j] >= k. Do not draw self-links.
choices.feedback: Correct. Meeting the threshold creates a usable secure line in both directions.

choices.label: Whenever `trust[i][j] > 0`, with low scores treated as weak edges.

pictureQuestions.prompt: For dials `[5, 1]`, `[4, 7]`, `[3]` with limit `9`, which complete code list is safe?

choices.label: Only code `[1, 4, 3]`
choices.feedback: Correct. 1+4+3 = 8 is the only total that stays at most 9.

choices.label: All four codes
choices.feedback: Every single weight is at most 9, but the lock adds them. Only 1+4+3 = 8 stays at most 9.

choices.label: Codes `[1, 4, 3]` and `[5, 4]`
choices.feedback: 5+4 = 9 lands on the limit after two dials, but the code is not finished. The last dial adds 3, and 12 busts.

choices.label: Codes `[1, 4, 3]`, `[1, 7, 3]`, and `[5, 4, 3]`
choices.feedback: These keep every code whose first two dials are safe. The last dial still adds 3: 1+7+3 = 11 and 5+4+3 = 12 both bust.

pictureQuestions.prompt: For dials `[4, 2]`, `[5]`, `[6, 9, 8]` with limit `12`, how many complete codes are safe?

choices.feedback: Correct. The smallest possible total is 2+5+6 = 13, which is over 12.
Every single weight is at most 12, but the lock adds them. Every full total is at least 13, so every code busts.

nodeQuestion.prompt: What is a node in the code-building decision tree?

choices.label: A safe partial code: the weights chosen on the first few dials, with total at most limit. The root is the empty code.
choices.feedback: Correct. Each level records one more dial choice, and the total comes from the weights on the path.

choices.label: One node per running total, so codes with the same total share a node.
choices.feedback: Different codes can reach the same total, like `3,4` and `4,3` when both dials offer 3 and 4. Each is its own answer, so each prefix needs its own node.

choices.label: Only a completed code using every dial.
choices.feedback: Completed codes are leaves. Partial-code nodes are needed to show the choices leading to them.

choices.label: One node per weight value, no matter which dial offered it.
choices.feedback: The same weight on different dials, or after different prefixes, is a different state. A node must remember the whole prefix.

edgeQuestion.prompt: When does a partial code have an edge to a longer code?

choices.label: Choose one weight from the next dial whose new running total is still at most limit.
choices.feedback: Correct. The edge appends one next-dial weight that does not bust.

choices.label: Choose any weight from the next dial that is at most limit by itself.
choices.feedback: The lock adds up every dial. A small weight can still push the running total over limit.

choices.label: Choose one weight from the next dial whose new running total is below limit.
choices.feedback: Landing exactly on limit is safe, like 21 in blackjack. Only going over busts.

choices.label: If every weight busts, skip to the following dial without adding a weight.
choices.feedback: A full code needs one weight from every dial. A prefix whose every choice busts has no child.

nodeQuestion.prompt: What is a node in the combination tree?

choices.label: A combination whose sum is at most limit. The root is the empty combination.
choices.feedback: Correct. Every node is a combination under the limit, so every node is part of the answer.

choices.label: One node per possible sum, so combinations with the same sum share a node.

edgeQuestion.prompt: When does a combination have an edge to a longer combination?

choices.label: Add one later number if the new sum is below limit.
choices.feedback: A sum exactly at the limit still counts. Only going over is left out.
